question: Which Plate defaults and public plugin contracts serve a product job, and which duplicate an adequate Plite owner?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; bounded first-principles lower-contract redesign comparison
trigger: User explicitly asks whether redesigning Plite extension to accommodate Plate plugin jobs could justify one plugin vocabulary and remove the adapter. This broadens the prior accessor/rename question to descriptor and composition ownership. Review only.
requirements: Reconsider the lower abstraction and the previous separate-accessor recommendation; current contracts and package topology are not hard laws.
Serve raw plugin capabilities and Plate product authoring on one canonical descriptor/composition protocol if that removes real translation.
Keep rendering, feature policy, product schema shorthand and contextual product compilation with Plate; raw Plite remains independently usable and headless.

Preserve contextual inference, prior-stage composition, configuration precedence and per-editor isolation, nominal ancestry, dependency/conflict semantics, candidate rollback and exact-view execution.
Preserve distinct document state versus runtime product state, source/configured/installed lifetimes and schema versus capability identity.
Identify actual deletion candidates and retained product work; do not replace both compilers with an opaque metadata bag or require feature authors to assemble low-level glue.
Record a provisional value verdict without product implementation or unsupported runtime/type-performance claims.
evidenceReuse: The prior September 13 accessor review matched source at intake but did not adequately consider one neutral composition/descriptor protocol with typed owner-specific contributions. The September 12 plan screened moving all product semantics into Plite; that is not the strongest shared-contract alternative. Reused its identity/lifetime requirements and historical receipts as context only. Rechecked raw contribution/descriptor APIs, Plate stage/configuration resolution and lowering, representative raw/headless/React consumers and existing assertion bodies. A bounded read-only worker mapped product compilation obligations, and the lead verified decisive references. No external discovery or executable proof was repeated.
summary: Pursue one neutral composable plugin descriptor shared by Plite and Plate, with typed Plate-owned declarations compiled against that same identity. This supersedes an isolated restoration of plugin/extension accessor names. Current Plate author stages, native/Plate capability branches, dependency remapping and creation of replacement defineExtension descriptors expose real deletion opportunities. Keep product compilation, schema semantics, runtime stores and view presentation in Plate; eliminate the second plugin engine and identity translation, not every product helper. A unified definePlugin/plugins/editor.plugin vocabulary becomes credible with that architecture. Runtime, type and adoption acceptance remain open; next owner is Task design plan shared plugin contract.
alternatives: Keep current contracts under extension: functional but preserves descriptor reconstruction and capability translation.

Restore plugin versus extension accessors: clearer for the current two-contract architecture, but does not remove the translation; superseded as the next isolated migration by the explicitly requested stronger design.
Rename extension to plugin without redesign: reject; vocabulary unification leaves the two engines intact.
Move the complete Plate plugin definition/compiler into Plite: reject; moves product policy and complexity into the substrate.

One neutral descriptor/composition engine with typed Plate contributions: strongest candidate; share identity and publication directly, remove dependency and native/Plate capability translation, preserve product compilation with its owner.
Force every caller to manually assemble raw contributions: reject as ordinary authoring because it exports product compilation/coordination to feature authors.
Introduce a generic metadata or metaframework layer: reject absent a concrete missing capability and net deletion. Existing typed contributions are the starting comparator, not assumed sufficient.
proofLimits: Source, consumer and assertion inspection only. No new prototype, tests, typechecks, browser or benchmark execution. Existing contribution tests establish the current ordered contribution contract, not typed product composition feasibility. Earlier reference/transaction measurements do not accept this larger target. Before adoption, prove one raw capability, one configured headless plugin and one React plugin on the shared protocol, including prior-stage inference, schema, state/configuration isolation, nominal dependencies, candidate rollback, view binding and static/SSR isolation. Compare construction/configuration/runtime lookup/update costs, retained state and declaration/type costs with the current owner. Require actual adapter/descriptor deletion; a wrapper around both compilers fails. Naming is proposed, not implemented.
